Lines.Text: Marin County’s libraries open their first VR stations.
A teen volunteer helps a first-time visitor into a headset.
XRLibraries launches as the pilot’s coordinator.
VR stations ship to libraries across California.
More than 90 libraries join, from the north coast to the border.
The Marin pilot becomes a statewide project.
Story time moves into virtual reality.
The youngest visitors hear stories inside 3D worlds.
Teens, meanwhile, head straight for the VR games.
Carson City Library reopens with VR and AR stations.
Nevada’s pilot puts 22 headsets in 11 libraries.
A visitor floats among planets and stars.
Marin’s VR program goes out into the community.
People displaced by deadly wildfires get a break.
Schools, senior centers and the county fair get visits too.
Librarians catalog VR so any library can find it.
Record by record, VR titles go into WorldCat.
More than 1,000 interactive 3D objects get cataloged.

Title: XR Marin and the XR Stars

Lines.Text: XR Marin teams libraries with schools.
Teen “XR Stars” help patrons with the gear.
A camper borrows the cameras to film her family’s farm.
Project SANDI brings VR job training to Nevada.
Trainees practice real tasks, like a dialysis technician’s.
It grows to more than 1,000 headsets at over 80 locations.
XRLibraries trains Washington librarians in 360° video.
Six libraries film 360° stories about their communities.
Put on a headset and you are standing in the story.
Lost Stories: young people rebuild overlooked history in XR.
Marin City students model the World War II shipyards.
Their music honors the African-American workers who built the ships.
A VR gallery of art by Ukrainian children opens online.
Anyone can walk through it free, in a web browser.
XRLibraries helped design the exhibition.
At the Marin County Fair, kids plant flowers in AR.
Monarch butterflies hatch and fly from flower to flower.
XRLibraries’ booth turns the fair into a pollinator garden.
